questions.prompt: Which activity did Art Aron say he and Elaine undertook together?
questions.promptZh: Art Aron说自己与Elaine共同做过哪项活动？
options: They used the same questionnaire instead of taking any trips.
They painted portraits only of strangers selected for a brain study.
They went rafting on the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon.
They trained sushi apprentices during their walking trips.
optionsZh: 用同一问卷替代所有旅行。
只给脑研究选出的陌生人画像。
在大峡谷的科罗拉多河漂流。
徒步旅行中培训寿司学徒。
analyses: A 原文列多个共同体验，未说问卷代替出行。
B each other指彼此画像，不是陌生人脑研究。
C rafted down the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon准确对应；信息来自采访中的个人叙述。
D 学徒是下一节Jiro的经历，不能移给Aron夫妇。

vocabulary.meaning: 认真采纳自己的研究发现；放在心上并实践
vocabulary.context: 在这段采访叙述里，夫妇把研究启发用于共同生活，并非说一段逸事单独验证所有研究结论。
vocabulary.example: They took their findings to heart by trying new activities together.

questions.evidenceQuote: In an interview, Art Aron said he and his wife, Elaine, took their findings to heart: They took walking trips in Japan, Italy, Serbia, and New Zealand. They painted pictures of each other, attended horse races, rafted down the Colorado River in the Grand Canyon, and went whale watching. Novelty is effective for long-term romantic couples, as is shared reflection.

questions.prompt: Which detail about the documentary is accurately stated?
questions.promptZh: 关于纪录片，哪项细节准确？
options: It is David Gelb's 2011 film about Jiro, who was then eighty-five.
It was made in 1965 about a forty-year-old chef opening his first restaurant.
It is a film by Jiro about Gelb's eighty-five years in Tokyo.
It describes Jiro as eighty-five at the time the website is opened.
optionsZh: 它是David Gelb的2011年影片，讲当时85岁的Jiro。
它摄于1965年，讲40岁厨师开第一家店。
它是Jiro拍摄Gelb在东京85年的影片。
它说打开网站时Jiro为85岁。
analyses: A David Gelb’s、2011、then eighty-five逐项对应。
B 把餐厅开业年份和年龄移到纪录片。
C 导演与被摄者颠倒，85修饰Jiro当时年龄。
D then指影片叙述的时间，不是当前网站访问日。

vocabulary.meaning: 当时；在所述那个时间点
vocabulary.context: then eighty-five-year-old将年龄锚定于纪录片语境，不能当作实时年龄。
vocabulary.example: The documentary follows a then eighty-five-year-old chef.

questions.evidenceQuote: Jiro Dreams of Sushi was the title of David Gelb’s 2011 documentary about Jiro Ono, a then eighty-five-year-old sushi chef in Tokyo. Jiro is obsessed with sushi, constantly trying to improve his techniques. He fusses about the temperature of sushi rice to the extreme; it must be the perfect temperature to maximize the taste of the fish. He uses a massage technique to make his octopus more tender.

questions.prompt: How does the sentence characterise Jiro's involvement with sushi?
questions.promptZh: 句子怎样描写Jiro对寿司的投入？
options: He has stopped improving because his techniques are already fixed.
He is interested only in teaching and no longer in his own cooking.
He experiments once and then avoids any further adjustment.
He is intensely absorbed in sushi and continually tries to improve his techniques.
optionsZh: 技法已固定，因此停止改进。
只关心教学，不再关心自己的烹调。
只试一次，此后避免调整。
高度投入寿司，持续尝试改善技法。
analyses: A constantly trying to improve与停止相反。
B 目标句明确关注his techniques，不能限成只教人。
C constantly表示持续，不是一次试完。
D obsessed与constantly trying共同描写强烈、不断的专注；这里不是临床诊断。

vocabulary.meaning: 痴迷的；专注到极强的程度
vocabulary.context: 此处为作者描述投入的用词，不足以推导精神疾病诊断。
vocabulary.example: The chef is obsessed with improving every detail of his craft.

questions.evidenceQuote: Jiro Dreams of Sushi was the title of David Gelb’s 2011 documentary about Jiro Ono, a then eighty-five-year-old sushi chef in Tokyo. Jiro is obsessed with sushi, constantly trying to improve his techniques. He fusses about the temperature of sushi rice to the extreme; it must be the perfect temperature to maximize the taste of the fish. He uses a massage technique to make his octopus more tender.

questions.prompt: What happened when Jiro tried massaging the octopus for longer?
questions.promptZh: Jiro尝试更长时间按摩章鱼后，文中说发生了什么？
options: Customers were measured as equally satisfied in a randomly assigned trial.
Customers seemed to enjoy the sushi more than before.
He reduced the original thirty minutes to an unspecified shorter time.
The passage says all customers disliked the longer preparation.
optionsZh: 随机试验测得顾客同样满意。
顾客似乎比以前更喜欢寿司。
他把原本30分钟缩为更短。
段落说所有顾客都不喜欢更长准备。
analyses: A experimented在此是厨师尝试，未写随机试验；seemed保留观察判断。
B even longer与seemed to enjoy...even more对应，保留似乎而非全员保证。
C longer方向与缩短相反。
D more不是disliked，且没有all customers的普遍量化。

vocabulary.meaning: 似乎；根据观察作出的保留判断
vocabulary.context: 这里描述顾客反应，不等同已进行严格随机试验或测出所有人的内心体验。
vocabulary.example: Customers seemed to enjoy the revised preparation more.

questions.evidenceQuote: He started off by massaging the octopus for thirty minutes; when he experimented with even longer massages, customers seemed to enjoy the sushi even more. Even though Jiro had already earned three Michelin stars with the thirty-minute massage, now he massages the octopus for forty-five minutes before cooking. He could have been satisfied with the methods he had already developed to get to the pinnacle of culinary art. Nonetheless, he always looks for ways to improve.

questions.prompt: How does 'could have been satisfied' contribute to the contrast?
questions.promptZh: could have been satisfied怎样构成对照？
options: It states that he actually stopped improving immediately after success.
It shows his earlier methods had never brought any recognition.
It presents resting on successful methods as a possibility, followed by his continued improvement.
It proves that satisfaction prevents every professional from changing any method.
optionsZh: 说他成功后确实立即停止改进。
说明以前方法从未带来认可。
提出本可满足于成功方法的可能，后接仍持续改进。
证明满足感使所有职业者都无法改变方法。
analyses: A could have不是已经如此，Nonetheless后文明确继续改善。
B 前文已有三星和pinnacle，非毫无认可。
C 本可满足与实际仍寻改进形成让步反差；不要把可能分支当既成行动。
D 个案叙述未建立所有职业者的必然规律。

vocabulary.meaning: 顶峰；很高成就的比喻
vocabulary.context: culinary art的pinnacle指烹饪技艺高成就，不是实际山峰或认为再无改进可能。
vocabulary.example: Reaching the pinnacle of a craft need not end the search for improvement.

questions.evidenceQuote: He started off by massaging the octopus for thirty minutes; when he experimented with even longer massages, customers seemed to enjoy the sushi even more. Even though Jiro had already earned three Michelin stars with the thirty-minute massage, now he massages the octopus for forty-five minutes before cooking. He could have been satisfied with the methods he had already developed to get to the pinnacle of culinary art. Nonetheless, he always looks for ways to improve.

questions.prompt: What feedback does Jiro attend to after each bite?
questions.promptZh: 每吃一口后，Jiro留意什么反馈？
options: Each customer's facial expressions.
Only a daily total of how many fish were bought.
An apprentice's written report before customers arrive.
Other chefs' competition scores displayed outside the restaurant.
optionsZh: 每位顾客的面部表情。
只看每天买鱼总数。
顾客到来前的学徒书面报告。
店外展示的其他厨师比赛分数。
analyses: A each customer’s facial expressions after each bite给观察对象与时间。
B 数量采购不是本句描写的顾客反馈。
C before与after时序不符，对象也换成学徒。
D 未写比赛分数，不能用其他段落的体育比较补造此情节。

vocabulary.meaning: 带着审视和评判的；不放过不足的
vocabulary.context: close and critical attention描述仔细评价顾客反应，不意味着他出言责骂顾客。
vocabulary.example: He pays critical attention to small changes in customers' expressions.

questions.evidenceQuote: He pays close and critical attention to each customer’s facial expressions after each bite. The selection of fish is as meticulous. His fifty-something son goes to the Tsukiji fish market to source all the ingredients from specialty merchants: shrimp from the same trusted shrimp merchant, eel from the same trusted eel merchant, and so forth. Every aspect of the preparation and cooking is exact, assessed every day, and improved over time.

questions.prompt: What does 'as meticulous' convey about selecting fish?
questions.promptZh: as meticulous怎样描写选鱼？
options: Fish selection receives less care because customer reactions matter more.
Fish is chosen casually once the rice temperature is correct.
The selection is meticulous only when ingredients are unfamiliar.
Fish selection is treated with similarly exacting care.
optionsZh: 因顾客反应更重要，选鱼反而少用心。
只要饭温对，鱼就随意选。
只有陌生食材才选得细。
选鱼同样受到严谨细致的对待。
analyses: A as承接相近的细致程度，没有less。
B meticulous不是casual，饭温的用心未抵消选料用心。
C 没有only unfamiliar条件，后句还提固定信任商家。
D The selection...as meticulous把同样细致扩展到食材选择。

vocabulary.meaning: 细致入微的；讲究每个细节的
vocabulary.context: 此处说选料的严谨程度，不是迟疑不决或仅按最低价格购买。
vocabulary.example: The selection of ingredients is as meticulous as the preparation.

questions.evidenceQuote: He pays close and critical attention to each customer’s facial expressions after each bite. The selection of fish is as meticulous. His fifty-something son goes to the Tsukiji fish market to source all the ingredients from specialty merchants: shrimp from the same trusted shrimp merchant, eel from the same trusted eel merchant, and so forth. Every aspect of the preparation and cooking is exact, assessed every day, and improved over time.

questions.prompt: How does Jiro's son obtain the ingredients in this account?
questions.promptZh: 这段描述中，Jiro儿子怎样采购食材？
options: He obtains shrimp and eel from a single unnamed general shop outside Tokyo.
He visits Tsukiji and uses trusted merchants specialising in the relevant ingredients.
He alternates suppliers randomly after every customer's bite.
He sends Jiro's apprentices to catch every ingredient personally.
optionsZh: 从东京外一间未具名综合店买虾和鳗。
到筑地，从相应食材的可信专门商家采购。
每位顾客吃一口就随机换供应商。
派学徒亲自捕获每种食材。
analyses: A specialty merchants为复数，且虾商、鳗商各有所专。
B Tsukiji、trusted、specialty三方面准确；fifty-something只表示五十多岁。
C same trusted merchant强调稳定信任，非随机轮换。
D source是采购获取，不是文中说儿子或学徒亲自捕捞。

vocabulary.meaning: 采购；寻找并取得供应
vocabulary.context: 这里为动词，指从专业商家获得食材，不是引用来源的名词义。
vocabulary.example: He visits specialist merchants to source fresh ingredients.

questions.evidenceQuote: He pays close and critical attention to each customer’s facial expressions after each bite. The selection of fish is as meticulous. His fifty-something son goes to the Tsukiji fish market to source all the ingredients from specialty merchants: shrimp from the same trusted shrimp merchant, eel from the same trusted eel merchant, and so forth. Every aspect of the preparation and cooking is exact, assessed every day, and improved over time.

questions.prompt: What does 'three to five apprentices at any given time' describe?
questions.promptZh: three to five apprentices at any given time描述什么？
options: A three-to-five-year training course for every apprentice.
Only three to five apprentices over his entire career.
A simultaneous group of roughly three to five trainees after he opened his restaurant.
Three to five restaurants opened before he began training anyone.
optionsZh: 每位学徒三至五年的课程。
他整个职业生涯总共只有三至五名学徒。
开店后同一时期约三至五人的受训群体。
开始教人前开了三至五家店。
analyses: A 数字单位是apprentices，不是years。
B at any given time限定同时规模，非终身总数。
C At that point承接40岁开店；同一时间有三至五人受训。
D 数字没有修饰餐厅数，不能移位。

vocabulary.meaning: 在任何一个给定时点；同一时期
vocabulary.context: 限定同时受训规模，不给整个生涯学徒总人数。
vocabulary.example: He trained a small group of apprentices at any given time.

questions.evidenceQuote: Because of war and poverty, Jiro left home at age nine. He did an apprenticeship in a sushi restaurant for many years, and finally opened up his own at age forty. At that point, he started training three to five apprentices at any given time. An apprentice starts out cleaning the restaurant and doing dishes.

questions.prompt: What work does an apprentice begin with?
questions.promptZh: 学徒先从什么工作开始？
options: Preparing tamago immediately on the first day.
Selecting every fish independently before learning restaurant work.
Opening a separate restaurant before being trained.
Cleaning the restaurant and washing dishes.
optionsZh: 第一天立即制作tamago。
未学店务就独立选全部鱼。
培训前先开独立餐厅。
清扫餐厅和洗碗。
analyses: A starts out明确清洁洗碗；tamago是后面的阶段。
B 本句没有先独立选鱼的安排。
C 开自己的店是后文的目标，非入门起点。
D cleaning the restaurant and doing dishes逐项给初始工作。

vocabulary.meaning: 开始时先做；起步
vocabulary.context: 这里是学徒训练起点，不是说永远只可清洁而无后续发展。
vocabulary.example: An apprentice starts out with basic restaurant duties.

questions.evidenceQuote: Because of war and poverty, Jiro left home at age nine. He did an apprenticeship in a sushi restaurant for many years, and finally opened up his own at age forty. At that point, he started training three to five apprentices at any given time. An apprentice starts out cleaning the restaurant and doing dishes.

questions.prompt: When does the account say an apprentice is finally allowed to cook tamago sushi?
questions.promptZh: 按这段叙述，学徒何时终于获准做tamago寿司？
options: After ten years of cleaning work.
After cooking exactly ten egg dishes on the first day.
As soon as the apprentice opens an independent restaurant.
Only after spending sixty years as head chef.
optionsZh: 做了十年清洁工作之后。
第一天恰做十份蛋料理之后。
学徒一开自己的店就可。
只有任主厨六十年之后。
analyses: A After ten years of cleaning work是文中明确时点，finally突出等待长。
B ten修饰years，不是料理份数；Nakazawa的两百份是另一细节。
C 学徒获准由Jiro允许，非先开店。
D sixty years来自Jiro长期职业的讨论，不是本段学徒许可时长。

vocabulary.meaning: 终于；经过漫长过程后才
vocabulary.context: 这里与十年清洁相连，强调进入下一阶段的迟缓，不保证该阶段已达满分。
vocabulary.example: After a long training period, the apprentice was finally allowed to cook the dish.
collocations: After ten years of cleaning work

questions.evidenceQuote: After ten years of cleaning work, Jiro finally allows an apprentice to cook a tamago sushi (egg custard sushi). Even Nakazawa, now a renowned sushi chef in New York, made two hundred tamagoyakis as an apprentice before Jiro finally deemed one usable. In the world of sushi shokunin (the professional sushi chef), as in any artisanal profession in Japan, there has always been a long and demanding training period. People go through this brutal apprenticeship because in the end they want to open up their own restaurants and succeed.

questions.prompt: What reason is given for enduring the demanding apprenticeship?
questions.promptZh: 文中给出的忍受艰苦学徒期的原因是什么？
options: The trainees are guaranteed a successful restaurant before they begin.
They ultimately want to open successful restaurants of their own.
They wish to avoid learning any specialised cooking technique.
They intend to spend their entire lives only washing dishes.
optionsZh: 开始前就保证给学徒一家成功餐厅。
最终想开自己的餐厅并成功。
想避免学习任何专门厨艺。
打算一生只洗碗。
analyses: A want表示目标，不是事前成功保证。
B because...in the end they want明确陈述动机，own restaurants为目标。
C 长期训练为专业技能，非避开。
D cleaning是起点，后文成功开店才是所述最终愿望。

vocabulary.meaning: 严酷的；极为苛刻难熬的
vocabulary.context: 此处形容训练强度与漫长，不足以单凭一词断言文中报道了具体肢体暴力。
vocabulary.example: The trainees endure a brutal apprenticeship in pursuit of their goal.
collocations: in the end they want to

questions.evidenceQuote: After ten years of cleaning work, Jiro finally allows an apprentice to cook a tamago sushi (egg custard sushi). Even Nakazawa, now a renowned sushi chef in New York, made two hundred tamagoyakis as an apprentice before Jiro finally deemed one usable. In the world of sushi shokunin (the professional sushi chef), as in any artisanal profession in Japan, there has always been a long and demanding training period. People go through this brutal apprenticeship because in the end they want to open up their own restaurants and succeed.

questions.prompt: Why are Phelps and Biles recalled at the start of this passage?
questions.promptZh: 这段开头回提Phelps与Biles有什么作用？
options: To establish that the documentary measured their cooking ability.
To show that neither had ever achieved excellence in sport.
To claim that every elite athlete has exactly the same mental-health history.
To set up a contrast between their loss of interest and Jiro's continued engagement.
optionsZh: 确立纪录片测量过他们厨艺。
说明两人在体育中从未出众。
声称每位顶尖运动员有完全相同心理健康经历。
引出他们失去兴趣与Jiro持续投入之间的比较。
analyses: A 本句回提第7章的体育经历，不是厨艺测量。
B sports they excelled at承认擅长；arguably还保留史上最佳的评价力度。
C 举两个人不能扩成every athlete，亦不是给所有人同一诊断。
D 紧接why didn’t Jiro also burn out把回顾用作比较问题的背景；这是作者在书中的叙述。

vocabulary.meaning: 擅长；在某领域表现出色
vocabulary.context: 此处强调成绩优秀与仍可能失去兴趣可以并存，不表示从未出色。
vocabulary.example: The passage discusses athletes who lost interest in sports they excelled at.

questions.evidenceQuote: In Chapter 7, I talked about how Michael Phelps and Simone Biles, arguably the best swimmer and gymnast of all time, suffered from depression and lost interest in the sports they excelled at. So, why didn’t Jiro also burn out after doing the same thing every day for over sixty years? First, Jiro’s quest for perfection is private and personal, whereas Phelps’s and Biles’s were public and in the context of competition with other athletes.

questions.prompt: What does the question about Jiro's burnout ask the reader to explain?
questions.promptZh: 关于Jiro倦怠的问句要求解释什么？
options: Why Jiro left home at the same age as both athletes.
Why decades of repeated work did not produce the same loss of engagement described in the comparison.
Why Jiro had no competitors at any point in his career.
Why all forms of repeated activity necessarily cause identical outcomes.
optionsZh: 为何Jiro与两位运动员同龄离家。
为何数十年重复工作没有出现对照中那种失去投入。
为何Jiro生涯从未有竞争者。
为何一切重复活动必然造成相同结果。
analyses: A 问句对象是burn out，非离家年龄。
B same thing every day for over sixty years与also burn out组成待解释反差，后面First开始给作者解释。
C 本段说private and personal，不能读成完全没有竞争者。
D 问句恰探讨不同结果，不建立重复必然同果的规律。

vocabulary.meaning: 倦怠；长期消耗后失去动力或兴趣
vocabulary.context: 此处承接长期工作与失去兴趣的比较，是书中解释主题，不由个案给读者诊断。
vocabulary.example: The author asks why the chef did not burn out after decades of work.
collocations: burn out after doing the same thing

questions.evidenceQuote: In Chapter 7, I talked about how Michael Phelps and Simone Biles, arguably the best swimmer and gymnast of all time, suffered from depression and lost interest in the sports they excelled at. So, why didn’t Jiro also burn out after doing the same thing every day for over sixty years? First, Jiro’s quest for perfection is private and personal, whereas Phelps’s and Biles’s were public and in the context of competition with other athletes.

questions.prompt: What second factor does the author introduce in explaining Jiro's engagement?
questions.promptZh: 解释Jiro投入时，作者引入的第二个因素是什么？
options: Diverse and unexpected challenges arising over time.
The permanent disappearance of every practical difficulty.
A fixed competition score published after every meal.
An unchanged supply of all ingredients throughout his career.
optionsZh: 随时间出现多样、意料外的挑战。
所有实际困难永久消失。
每餐后公布固定比赛分数。
生涯中全部食材供应从未变化。
analyses: A Second...diverse, unexpected challenges明确给第二项，后句举鱼类供应变化。
B faced challenges与困难消失相反。
C 公开比赛成绩属于前面的运动员对比，不是Jiro面临的此项因素。
D 后句正说some fish disappeared，不能说供给全无变化。

vocabulary.meaning: 多样的；不同类型的
vocabulary.context: 与unexpected共同限定他面临的挑战，不仅是同一项困难被机械重复。
vocabulary.example: The chef faced diverse challenges as his environment changed.

questions.evidenceQuote: What is so tough about being an elite athlete is that every defeat is objectively recorded and becomes public. While Jiro has had many competitors, Jiro’s performance was not closely watched against the performances of others. Second, like all sushi chefs in Japan, Jiro faced diverse, unexpected challenges over time. As some popular sushi fish disappeared from Tokyo Bay, Jiro had to adjust the type of sushi he served over the years.

questions.prompt: Why did Jiro have to adjust the kinds of sushi he served?
questions.promptZh: Jiro为何不得不调整所供应的寿司种类？
options: The documentary required him to imitate the athletes' training routines.
Every customer refused all fish on a single recorded day.
Some popular sushi fish disappeared from Tokyo Bay.
His son stopped visiting every specialist merchant permanently.
optionsZh: 纪录片要求他模仿运动员训练。
某个有记录的日子所有顾客拒绝全部鱼。
东京湾某些常用寿司鱼类消失。
儿子永久停止拜访所有专门商家。
analyses: A 未写纪录片这样要求，不能给菜单变化另造起因。
B some fish不等于every customer/all fish，也无单日全员拒绝。
C As引出供应环境的变化，had to adjust给其后果，范围是some popular fish。
D 可信商家的采购描述不表示儿子退出采购。

vocabulary.meaning: 调整；因情况变化改变做法
vocabulary.context: 这里改变所供应寿司种类以应对鱼类供应变化，不一定放弃寿司职业。
vocabulary.example: He had to adjust the menu as the available fish changed.

questions.evidenceQuote: What is so tough about being an elite athlete is that every defeat is objectively recorded and becomes public. While Jiro has had many competitors, Jiro’s performance was not closely watched against the performances of others. Second, like all sushi chefs in Japan, Jiro faced diverse, unexpected challenges over time. As some popular sushi fish disappeared from Tokyo Bay, Jiro had to adjust the type of sushi he served over the years.

questions.prompt: What result of the environmental changes is stated here?
questions.promptZh: 此处明确说环境变化带来什么结果？
options: He no longer needed to make daily decisions.
His menu stayed exactly as it had been at the start.
He stopped preparing sushi and became a competitive athlete.
He was compelled to change the way he created his menu.
optionsZh: 他不再需要每日做决定。
菜单与开始时完全一样。
他不再做寿司，转成竞技运动员。
他被迫改变制定菜单的方式。
analyses: A 本段反而说preoccupied with various daily decisions and demands。
B have forced him to change明确不是始终不变。
C change the way he creates his menu不是换职业。
D 环境变化为主语，forced...change给明确影响；无需把它扩成所有因素只有环境。

vocabulary.meaning: 迫使；使不得不作改变
vocabulary.context: 此处为外部条件使他调整菜单，不是说他完全不能再作任何选择。
vocabulary.example: Changing supplies forced the chef to reconsider his menu.
collocations: the way he creates his menu

questions.evidenceQuote: All these environmental changes have forced him to change the way he creates his menu. These challenges as well as economic challenges keep him on his toes. Whereas some elite athletes tend to ruminate on their performance and need to motivate themselves to train hard every day, Jiro has been preoccupied with various daily decisions and demands. Because of all the challenges, he hasn’t had time to really ruminate on his mistakes (I assume even a master makes them now and then).

questions.prompt: How does the passage connect challenges with rumination on mistakes?
questions.promptZh: 段落怎样联系挑战与对错误的反复琢磨？
options: It proves that a master never makes any mistake.
It claims challenges occupy Jiro's time, while the narrator explicitly marks the occasional mistakes as an assumption.
It gives a measured count of every mistake Jiro made each day.
It says Jiro spends more time brooding than making daily decisions.
optionsZh: 证明大师从不犯错。
说挑战占据Jiro时间，同时作者明确把偶尔犯错标为自己的假定。
给出Jiro每天每次错误的实测计数。
说Jiro反刍比日常决策更久。
analyses: A I assume even a master makes them恰不支持从不犯错。
B hasn’t had time与I assume分别是解释及括注的认识限定，不能改成全面心理测量。
C now and then不是逐次计数，assume也非测得。
D hasn’t had time to really ruminate和preoccupied with decisions方向相反；不能由此推出任何挑战都治好所有人的反刍。

vocabulary.meaning: 反复琢磨；在心中一再回想
vocabulary.context: 此处对象为mistakes，带反复纠结的含义，不是一般的迅速检查或反刍动物消化。
vocabulary.example: He had little time to ruminate on mistakes while making daily decisions.

questions.evidenceQuote: All these environmental changes have forced him to change the way he creates his menu. These challenges as well as economic challenges keep him on his toes. Whereas some elite athletes tend to ruminate on their performance and need to motivate themselves to train hard every day, Jiro has been preoccupied with various daily decisions and demands. Because of all the challenges, he hasn’t had time to really ruminate on his mistakes (I assume even a master makes them now and then).

questions.prompt: What does 'Third' introduce about Jiro?
questions.promptZh: Third引入Jiro的哪个特点？
options: A third Michelin star earned on the day of the documentary.
A third restaurant opened after he abandoned sushi.
Playfulness as another part of the author's explanation.
A third experimental group assigned to a playful activity.
optionsZh: 拍纪录片当天获得第三颗米其林星。
放弃寿司后开的第三家店。
把玩心作为作者解释的另一部分。
分到玩耍活动的第三个实验组。
analyses: A Third为论述序号，不是获星当天的事件次序。
B 目标句没有开第三家店或放弃寿司。
C Third...Jiro is playful给第三项解释，并回连Chapter 7主题，后句以朋友回忆和与顾客说笑展开。
D 这是个案描述与作者分析，没有第三实验组的设计。

vocabulary.meaning: 有玩心的；轻松而爱逗趣的
vocabulary.context: 和后文lightheartedness、joking呼应，不等于不认真对待专业技艺。
vocabulary.example: The author describes the meticulous chef as playful as well.

questions.evidenceQuote: Third, going back to the theme of Chapter 7, Jiro is playful. He was a very mischievous boy, according to an interview with his elementary school friends in the documentary. He has carried his sense of lightheartedness well into his eighties, still joking around with his customers.

questions.prompt: What possibility does the conditional sentence about the menu describe?
questions.promptZh: 关于菜单的条件句描述什么可能？
options: If boredom occurs, he can invent new nigiri or new ways of cooking eel within his craft.
Because the menu never changes, he has no possible response to boredom.
He must leave sushi entirely before he can try any new technique.
He has already tried every possible dish and has no remaining creative choices.
optionsZh: 若感到无聊，他可在厨艺内部创作新握寿司或鳗鱼新做法。
因菜单从不变，他对无聊毫无办法。
必须完全离开寿司，才可试新技法。
已试尽所有可能料理，再无创作选择。
analyses: A if he ever gets bored为条件，can come up with说明可在同一领域创新，并不确认他此刻正在无聊。
B any number of ways与无可能相反。
C 新握寿司和新鳗鱼做法均留在寿司创作内。
D any number of ways强调多种选择，非所有可能已经穷尽。

vocabulary.meaning: 现有的；当前存在的
vocabulary.context: extant menu指已有菜单，与他可新创的项目对照，不是已经失传的菜单。
vocabulary.example: He could invent a new dish if he became bored with the extant menu.
collocations: come up with any number of ways

questions.evidenceQuote: After all, sushi is a creative art. Jiro can come up with any number of ways to create a new nigiri or a new way to cook eel if he ever gets bored with the extant menu. He thinks that he can still improve as a sushi chef. Jiro opened Sukiyabashi Jiro in 1965.

questions.prompt: Which event is dated 1965 in the passage?
questions.promptZh: 段落把哪件事标为1965年？
options: David Gelb released the documentary.
Jiro turned eighty-five during filming.
The author opened a restaurant in New York.
Jiro opened Sukiyabashi Jiro.
optionsZh: David Gelb发行纪录片。
Jiro拍摄时满85岁。
作者在纽约开餐厅。
Jiro开设Sukiyabashi Jiro。
analyses: A 纪录片年份在前文是2011，不是1965。
B then85属于纪录片语境，未与1965相连。
C 主语为Jiro，店名明确，不能换作者及纽约。
D opened...in1965直接给事件与时间；只按书中叙述答题，不把它当实时营业信息。

vocabulary.meaning: 开设；开始经营
vocabulary.context: 这里是创办餐厅的事件，不是日常当天打开门营业，也非纪录片首映。
vocabulary.example: He opened the restaurant in 1965, according to the passage.

questions.evidenceQuote: After all, sushi is a creative art. Jiro can come up with any number of ways to create a new nigiri or a new way to cook eel if he ever gets bored with the extant menu. He thinks that he can still improve as a sushi chef. Jiro opened Sukiyabashi Jiro in 1965.

questions.prompt: What continuity does the opening sentence emphasise?
questions.promptZh: 开头句强调哪方面的持续性？
options: Changing the restaurant's location and head chef every few years.
Serving for a long time as head chef at the same restaurant and location.
Having no work responsibilities during most of the period.
Giving a different restaurant a new name each day.
optionsZh: 每几年更换餐厅地点与主厨。
长期在同一地点、同一家店任主厨。
这时期大部分时间没有工作职责。
每天给另一餐厅改名。
analyses: A same restaurant、same location明确强调相同，非轮换。
B long time、head chef及两次same给角色、时间与地点的持续性；无需由本段外补算年数。
C head chef为工作角色，非大部分没有职责。
D 未有每日改名的叙述。

vocabulary.meaning: 主厨；负责厨房工作的厨师
vocabulary.context: 这里强调长期担任的职业角色，不是身体部位或餐厅顾客。
vocabulary.example: He remained head chef at the same restaurant for many years.
collocations: the head chef of the same restaurant

questions.evidenceQuote: That is a long time to be the head chef of the same restaurant in the same location. But even after so many years, he hates holidays when he has to close his restaurant. He always looks forward to working at his restaurant. Even if you do the same things every day for many decades, you can still find something new to try regularly.

questions.prompt: Why are holidays presented negatively in Jiro's account?
questions.promptZh: Jiro的叙述为何负面提到假期？
options: They require him to change the restaurant's location permanently.
They force every customer to become an apprentice.
They are times when he has to close the restaurant despite his continued desire to work.
They prove that he no longer enjoys cooking and wants to retire.
optionsZh: 假期要求他永久换店址。
假期迫使每个顾客当学徒。
假期必须关店，而他仍希望工作。
假期证明他不再爱烹调而想退休。
analyses: A close是关门停业，不等于永久搬迁。
B 本句没有顾客变学徒的要求。
C hates holidays when he has to close承接长期工作却仍期待工作的反差。
D 下句looks forward to working与不再喜欢和想退休相反。

vocabulary.meaning: 关门停业；暂不营业
vocabulary.context: 在假期语境中不自动表示永久歇业、搬迁或结束职业生涯。
vocabulary.example: He disliked holidays when he had to close the restaurant.

questions.evidenceQuote: That is a long time to be the head chef of the same restaurant in the same location. But even after so many years, he hates holidays when he has to close his restaurant. He always looks forward to working at his restaurant. Even if you do the same things every day for many decades, you can still find something new to try regularly.

questions.prompt: What does 'looks forward to working' mean here?
questions.promptZh: looks forward to working在此是什么意思？
options: He expects restaurant work with positive anticipation.
He dreads returning to work and tries to postpone it.
He looks physically toward the front of the building while standing still.
He is certain that no new task will ever arise in the restaurant.
optionsZh: 他怀着积极期待盼望到餐厅工作。
他害怕复工，试图拖延。
他站着朝建筑前方望去。
他确信店里永远不会有新任务。
analyses: A look forward to是盼望；to后working是动名词，指期待工作这件事。
B 与积极期待相反，且hates holidays也支持他愿工作。
C 固定表达不能逐词读成物理朝前看。
D 期待工作并不宣称以后全无新任务，段末还说可找到新尝试。

vocabulary.meaning: 期待；盼望某事或做某事
vocabulary.context: to在这一固定表达中是介词，所以接working；并非朝前方观看。
vocabulary.example: He looks forward to working with new ingredients.

questions.evidenceQuote: That is a long time to be the head chef of the same restaurant in the same location. But even after so many years, he hates holidays when he has to close his restaurant. He always looks forward to working at his restaurant. Even if you do the same things every day for many decades, you can still find something new to try regularly.

questions.prompt: What reason distinguishes a shokunin's work from an amateur's in the sentence?
questions.promptZh: 句子用什么理由区分shokunin与业余者的工作？
options: It guarantees the same menu without any changes in technique.
It requires lifetime devotion.
It allows only a brief interest before the worker must stop.
It depends on changing careers whenever a familiar task appears.
optionsZh: 保证菜单不变、技法毫无变化。
它要求终身投入。
只容许短暂兴趣，随后必须停止。
取决于一遇熟悉任务就换职业。
analyses: A 当前句给理由是lifetime devotion，不是保证技法永不变。
B because it requires lifetime devotion明确给差别的原因。
C lifetime与brief interest相反。
D Jiro例子是专注深入，不是遇熟悉即转行；本题仅按该句的区别作答。

vocabulary.meaning: 投入；持续专注与献身
vocabulary.context: lifetime限定长期程度，不能据此保证每个人的职业道路都相同或都成功。
vocabulary.example: The craft requires years of sustained devotion.

questions.evidenceQuote: The work of a shokunin, like Jiro, is different from that of an amateur because it requires lifetime devotion.
